identity.name: Myinsaing Kingdom
native_names: မြင်စိုင်းပြည် (Myinsaing Pyi)

land.text: the Dry Zone around Myinsaing, Kyaukse and Minbu, taken by the three brothers when they overthrew Kyawswa on 17 December 1297

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Myinsaing from 1294 inside Pagan's 1293 shape (669 of 672 cells); the pagan-kingdom dossier (se-01-c) ends Pagan on 17 December 1297.

land.text: the same 672 cells: Cliopatria's Pinya shape of 1314 is identical

successors.note: Thihathu, the last brother, founded Pinya on 7 February 1313 ('Pinya founded: 7 February 1313'); the Sagaing secession of 15 May 1315 follows. One polity and dynasty under a new capital; kept apart because Cliopatria and the Wikipedia infobox list Pinya as the successor.

capitals.name: Myinsaing
capitals.note: Infobox lists 'Myinsaing, Mekkhaya, Pinle' without years; the coordinates are approximate (near Meiktila), the page gives none.

rulers.name: Athinkhaya, Yazathingyan and Thihathu (the three brothers)
rulers.title: joint rulers
rulers.note: Infobox '1297-1310: Athinkhaya, Yazathingyan, Thihathu'; Athinkhaya died 1305/06 in some chronicles; Thihathu 'proclaimed himself king' on 20 October 1309.

rulers.name: Thihathu
rulers.note: Sole ruler, founder of Pinya on 7 February 1313.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies from December 1297 to 1304

keyframe_review.note: Years only: December 1297-1304. 193,597 km2 (672 cells: Mandalay 129, Magway 109, Sagaing 124, Shan 193, Bago 90) and 669 of them inside Cliopatria's Pagan shape of 1293, so 1294-1297 would double-draw Pagan; the brothers 'overthrew King Kyawswa on 17 December 1297'. Page extent: 'from Tagaung in the north to Prome to the south', with 'several Shan states' dominating the rest of the arc and Martaban holding 'the south beyond Prome and Toungoo'; the shape's 193 Shan-hill cells are therefore a generous claim. No infobox area to compare.

The same 672 cells as 1294 (identical shape); no dated territorial change in 1305 on the page (Athinkhaya died 1305/06 in some chronicles, Thihathu took a royal title in 1306). Holds to the founding of Pinya on 7 February 1313.

region.text: the Dry Zone 'from Tagaung in the north to Prome to the south'

ledger.note: 17 December 1297: the three Myinsaing brothers overthrow Kyawswa and take over Pagan's heartland. 'The brothers overthrew King Kyawswa on 17 December 1297, with help from the dowager queen Pwa Saw'; the kingdom 'ran from Tagaung in the north to Prome to the south'. The page names the span, not a boundary; Cliopatria's shape is used.

region.text: Singu and Male, the Mongol garrisons north of Myinsaing

ledger.note: January 1300: Athinkhaya's army seizes Mongol garrisons at Singu and Male. The Yuan emperor backed Kumara Kassapa on 22 June 1300 and ordered an invasion; the Mongols 'managed to reach Myinsaing on 25 January 1301' and called off the attack on 6 April 1301 after a bribe.
4 April 1303: the Mongols withdraw from northern Burma. 'The Mongols withdrew from northern Burma on 4 April 1303.'

region.text: the Dry Zone from Kyaukse and Minbu to the Mu valley

ledger.note: 1303: after the Mongol withdrawal the brothers take the Kyaukse, Minbu and Mu granaries. 'After the 1303 withdrawal, the brothers took the Kyaukse, Minbu, and Mu granaries.' The page does not say whether the Yuan or nobody held them.

region.text: the Myinsaing kingdom, which Pinya inherits cell for cell

ledger.note: 7 February 1313: Thihathu founds Pinya and Myinsaing ends. Infobox 'Pinya founded: 7 February 1313', Yazathingyan having died in 1312/13; Pinya is the successor and, from 15 May 1315, Sagaing splits off to the north.

wars.name: Mongol campaign against Myinsaing (1300-1303)
wars.outcome: The Mongols reached Myinsaing on 25 January 1301, called off the attack on 6 April 1301 after a bribe and withdrew from northern Burma on 4 April 1303.
wars.note: The emperor backed Kumara Kassapa as king on 22 June 1300. The Pagan dossier (se-01-c) carries the earlier Yuan occupation of northern Burma to Tagaung from 1284.

certainty.note: The Dry Zone core is firm; the Shan-hill edge and the Prome and Toungoo south are approximate, with Shan states and Martaban beside it.

sources.title: Myinsaing Kingdom
sources.note: Infobox, 17 December 1297, the Mongol campaign 1300-1303, extent, Pinya 1313.

notes:
Start moved from Cliopatria's 1294 to 17 December 1297 (the brothers' takeover, Myinsaing page) and end set to 7 February 1313 (Pinya founded; Cliopatria 1313). One page was opened (the budget is 1-2); no area on it. Cliopatria's two shapes (1294-1304, 1305-1313) are the same 672 cells, which are also the whole of its Pinya shape of 1314, so Myinsaing and Pinya are one polity and dynasty under a new capital; a merge under the earlier slug is possible if the Pinya dossier agrees. The Myinsaing shape includes 193 Shan-hill cells that the page assigns to the Shan states; the pagan-kingdom, shan-states and kingdom-of-pinya dossiers should agree on this land.
Counterpart for the 1303 gain: the page does not say who held the granaries. The capital's coordinates (21.2 N, 95.85 E) are approximate and unsourced (the page gives none); the infobox also lists Mekkhaya and Pinle as capitals without years. The page has Temür Khan recognise Kyawswa as King of Burma on 20 March 1297 (before the overthrow) and says nothing of a Yuan recognition of the brothers.
